sentences.text: Cryonectes was a moderate-sized pliosaurid with a skull measuring 47 centimeters in length.
This animal featured a greatly elongated snout that was slightly constricted, along with a long lower jaw symphysis containing seven tooth positions and a distinct ventral ridge.
The genus name Cryonectes translates to 'cold swimmer,' honoring the cool climate of the time.
Its species name, neustriacus, honors the Frank kingdom of Neustria located in northwest France.
The fossil was collected in the 1980s from the Roche-Blain quarry near Laize-la-Ville in Normandy, France.
The genus is known only from the holotype MAE 2007.1.1(J), which consists of a partial skull, an articulated mandible, and ten associated vertebrae.
Peggy Vincent, Nathalie Bardet, and Emanuela Mattioli named the genus in 2012, establishing Cryonectes neustriacus as the type species.
Evidence suggests the specimen was a subadult individual at a relatively early stage of development.
Cryonectes is classified within the family Pliosauridae.
Cladistic analysis places Cryonectes as basal to Pliosaurus, Peloneustes, and other pliosaurids.
The authority for the genus Cryonectes is listed as Vincent, Bardet & Mattioli, 2013.
Cryonectes lived during the Early Jurassic period, specifically the upper Pliensbachian stage.
The time range for Cryonectes is estimated between 192.9 and 184.2 million years ago.
